fieldMarks: Very large, mule-like ears about three-quarters the length of the head.
Narrow white tail with a black tip, and a white rump patch.
Bucks' antlers fork (bifurcate) and re-fork rather than growing points off one main beam.
Reddish-brown summer coat, brownish-gray in winter; a dark V mark on the forehead, most visible on bucks.
behavior: Escapes with a bounding gait; releases metatarsal scent that alerts other deer.
Females live in clans; bucks form separate groups.
Selective browser of leaves and twigs of shrubs and trees, plus acorns, legume seeds and fruit.
Migrates from high summer range to lower winter range; rut peaks late November to mid-December.
habitat: Deserts, grasslands, chaparral, forests and mountains of western North America.
range: Western North America west of about the 100th meridian (roughly 23°–60° N), from southwestern Saskatchewan through the Great Plains to western Texas, with isolated populations in Minnesota, Iowa and Missouri.

lookalikes.name: White-tailed deer
lookalikes.howToTell: White-tails have a broad tail raised as a white flag when alarmed, and antler points rising from one main beam.

lookalikes.name: Black-tailed deer
lookalikes.howToTell: Black-tailed deer have a completely black or dark brown tail and occur west of the Great Divide.
